hints: Use the binomial coefficients for powers $y^0$, $y^1$ and $y^2$; stop after the quadratic term.
walkthrough:
Apply the binomial theorem to expand $(1 + y)^6$ up to $y^2$:
$$(1 + y)^6 = 1 + \binom{6}{1}y + \binom{6}{2}y^2 + \dots = 1 + 6y + 15y^2$$

Substitute $y = px - 2x^2$ into the expansion from part (i):
$$(1 + px - 2x^2)^6 = 1 + 6(px - 2x^2) + 15(px - 2x^2)^2 + \dots$$
$$= 1 + 6px - 12x^2 + 15(p^2 x^2 - 4px^3 + 4x^4) + \dots$$

Extract and collect the terms containing $x^2$:
$$\text{Term in } x^2 = -12x^2 + 15p^2 x^2 = (15p^2 - 12)x^2$$

Equate the coefficient to $48$ and solve for the positive constant $p$:
$$15p^2 - 12 = 48 \implies 15p^2 = 60 \implies p^2 = 4 \implies p = 2 \quad (\text{since } p > 0)$$
